entities.name: Eannatum II
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Eannatum II, son of Entemena, was Ensi (governor) of Lagash.

Born around 2500 BCE in Sumer, Lagash, and died before 2450 BCE, Eannatum II rose to power during the Early Dynastic Period of Sumer. As Ensi, he implemented significant administrative and territorial reforms, including the creation of a standardized system of weights and measures, and the construction of extensive irrigation canals. He also strengthened the city's defenses and increased its trade connections. Through his policies, Eannatum II solidified Lagash's position as a major power in Sumer and secured its place in the annals of Sumerian history.

His legacy can be seen in the numerous inscriptions and artifacts left behind, including the famous Stele of the Vultures, which commemorates his military campaigns and administrative achievements. Eannatum II's impact extends beyond his own city, as his reforms and policies influenced the development of Sumerian civilization as a whole.

The impact of Eannatum II's reign is still felt today, as his legacy serves as a testament to the ingenuity and resilience of the Sumerians, who were able to adapt to the challenges of their environment and build a thriving civilization in the face of adversity.
